selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of T cells across murine lymphoid, mucosal, and gland tissues
papers.authors: Wang, X.; Pei, B.; Liu, J.; Han, Z.; Wang, X.; Wang, Y.; Zhao, X.
papers.abstract: T cells play essential roles in immune surveillance, host defense, and tissue homeostasis, with their cellular composition and transcriptional states varying across tissues. In this study, we constructed an integrated single-cell transcriptional atlas of 124,186 T cells from seven organs of healthy mice. We identified shared T cell states with distinct tissue associated distributions and transcriptional features. Further analyses revealed transcriptional changes associated with thymocyte maturation, diverse innate-like and memory-like T cell populations in bone marrow, and distinct regional distributions of CD8-like T cell states in the intestine. The submandibular gland contained diverse naive, helper-associated, and effector-associated T cell states. pySCENIC analysis further revealed tissue associated variation in inferred transcription factor regulon activity within shared T cell populations. Together, these findings provide a single cell reference for understanding T cell heterogeneity across lymphoid and non-lymphoid tissues under physiological conditions.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis identifies concurrent type 2 and interferon programs in experimental eosinophilic esophagitis
papers.authors: Dsilva, A.; Handler, K.; Baron, T.; Itan, M.; Avlas, S.; Zan Bar, I.; Varol, C.; Rothenberg, M.; Arnold, I. C.; Munitz, A.
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, type 2 cytokine-driven allergic disease of the esophagus. How the immune and structural cell landscape of the esophagus changes between healthy and inflamed tissue requires further investigation. Methods: CD45-enriched esophageal cells from naive and oxazolone (OXA)-challenged wild-type mice were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. A cytokine-gated gene expression score identified type 2 program-high cells. Findings were compared with published human esophageal datasets, validated histologically, and examined in Il13ra1-/- mice. Results: A total of 62,245 esophageal cells were analyzed. ILC2s accounted for most type 2 cytokine-expressing lymphocytes in naive mice, whereas Th2 cells accounted for approximately 80% following OXA challenge. ILC2s concurrently lost Il5, Il13 and Gata3 expression while retaining Areg. Resident memory-like CD8 T cells became the largest lymphoid population. Mast cells switched from a connective tissue-type to a mucosal-type and partly cycling state, which was confirmed by increased MCPT1 cells. Esophageal eosinophils displayed a signature resembling skin eosinophils of atopic dermatitis rather than gastrointestinal eosinophils. Il13ra1-/- mice were protected from epithelial proliferation, thickening and eosinophilia. An interferon-associated program characterized lymphoid, myeloid and structural compartments, and its epithelial component was conserved in human EoE. Conclusions: Th2 cells and mucosal-type mast cells are the dominant sources of type 2 cytokines in experimental EoE. This study further identifies a conserved interferon-associated program that accompanies the type 2 response in the immune and structural compartments of the esophagus and highlights it as a candidate contributor to EoE pathology.

papers.title: scCVD: a comprehensive single-cell omics atlas of cerebrovascular disease.
papers.authors: Zhou LW, Qian FC, Li D, Wang QY, Wang H, Li BL, Guan QB, Wang Q, Yin K, Liu J, Sun Y, Li CQ, Zhu YB, Hu BY.
papers.abstract: Cerebrovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Initially insulting the cerebral vasculature, CVD pathology engages the entire neurovascular unit, including endothelial and mural cells, astrocytes, microglia, neurons, and the perivascular fibroblasts and infiltrating peripheral immune cells. Single-cell studies over CVD have generated enormous scattered and heterogeneously annotated atlases, which never supplement an organized visualization and an integrated analysis. Here, we present scCVD (https://scportal.cn/sccvd), an integrated single-cell database of scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data for CVD that characterises expression patterns and chromatin accessibility of CVD-related genes across diverse cell types and disease stages. The current release comprises 701 high-quality samples from four species (human, mouse, rat, and marmoset), encompassing over 4.68 million cells. All datasets were manually curated and standardized, with harmonised metadata covering disease versus control status, disease time points and experimental interventions. scCVD provides analysis modules for differential expression, functional enrichment, trajectory inference, cell-cell communication, transcription factor regulatory networks, and chromatin accessibility, together with interactive visualisation. scCVD also supports convenient data browsing and retrieval, customisable online analysis and batch download, facilitating systematic investigation of cellular heterogeneity and molecular regulatory mechanisms in CVD.

papers.title: The immune microenvironment in MDS-to-AML transformation: dynamic ecological remodeling and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Long Z, Wu R, Yuan S, Yang K, Cheng T, Han B, Yang J.
papers.abstract: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal myeloid neoplasms characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis, cytopenias, and a variable risk of transformation to Acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although genetic lesions are central to MDS pathogenesis, progression to AML cannot be explained by mutation accumulation alone. This review synthesizes evidence that MDS-to-AML transformation is a dynamic ecological process driven by reciprocal interactions between mutant hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell clones and the bone marrow immune microenvironment. In normal marrow, hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, T cells, NK(natural killer) cells, myeloid cells, mesenchymal stromal cells, endothelial cells, and the extracellular matrix maintain hematopoietic homeostasis and immune surveillance. In MDS, chronic inflammation coexists with impaired immune effector function, including T-cell exhaustion, reduced NK-cell cytotoxicity, expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and immunosuppressive regulatory T-cell subsets, monocyte-macrophage reprogramming, mesenchymal stromal cell dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, and metabolic adaptation. Together, these alterations establish a proinflammatory but immunosuppressive niche that weakens clearance of abnormal clones while providing stromal and metabolic support for clonal expansion and treatment resistance. Mutant clones further remodel the niche through epigenetic silencing, altered chemokine and cytokine signaling, and inflammatory-metabolic reprogramming, generating positive-feedback circuits that link inflammation, DNA damage, immune escape, increasing clonal burden, and therapy resistance. This review discusses how integrating clonal genetics with immune, stromal, and metabolic features may refine risk stratification and inform microenvironment-directed combination therapies. Longitudinal single-cell and spatial profiling will be essential for identifying reversible immune dysfunction and developing individualized strategies to delay or prevent AML transformation.

papers.title: Dual-targeting BCMA/CD19 CAR T cells with asymmetric 4-1BB/CD28-YMFM costimulation in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: a phase 1/2 trial with single-cell profiling of extramedullary disease.
papers.authors: Jiang H, Li L, Yang C, Chen K, Xie L, Ma R, Lu Y, He C, Feng F, Mei X, Wu H, Chen X, Li D, Xiao X, Cai X, Zhou T, Yuan H, Zhou Z, Ye X, Zhao J, Guan T, Ma L, Bai M, Wu G, Su L, Fu W.
papers.abstract: Background Extramedullary disease (EMD) predicts poor outcomes after B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). KQ-2003 is a bicistronic BCMA/CD19 CAR T-cell product incorporating 4-1BB and CD28-YMFM costimulatory domains. We assessed its activity and intralesional biology, focusing on EMD. Methods Twenty-four patients received KQ-2003 (21 trial participants; three compassionate-use patients). Hematologic and EMD responses were assessed using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) and Italian Myeloma criteria for PET Use, respectively. Bone marrow minimal residual disease (MRD) was assessed by next-generation flow cytometry (10 - 5 sensitivity). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. Longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing profiled one patient's infusion product, serial blood, and spatially distinct EMD biopsies. Results Patients had received a median of five prior lines; 18 (75.0%) were triple-class refractory, six (25.0%) penta-refractory, 23 (95.8%) had high-risk cytogenetics, and 15 (62.5%) had EMD. All 20 patients with measurable hematologic disease achieved hematologic responses (18 [90.0%] complete/stringent complete); IMWG-defined overall response rate was 95.0%. Fourteen (93.3%) of 15 EMD patients achieved metabolic responses (13 [86.7%] complete). Among 19 baseline MRD-positive patients, 12 (63.2%) became MRD-negative by month 6; 10 and six also had documented negativity at months 12 and 24, respectively. At 29.2 months' median follow-up, median PFS was 24.0 months (95% CI, 15.0-not reached); no significant difference was detected by baseline EMD status (HR, 0.92; P = 0.89). Among the 21 trial participants, grade ≥ 3 cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in one (4.8%) and two (9.5%), respectively; two treatment-related fatal pneumonias occurred. Single-patient longitudinal profiling revealed proliferating lesion-infiltrating CAR T cells with increased CCL3/CCL4 expression and tumor-cell apoptotic and necroptotic transcriptional programs. Trajectory analysis suggested transcriptional links between tissue effectors and circulating CCL5-positive memory-like CAR T cells. CellChat predicted BCMA-related tumor-microenvironment interactions and immune-cell interactions involving circulating CAR T cells. Conclusions KQ-2003 produced deep, durable hematologic and metabolic responses in heavily pretreated, high-risk RRMM, including EMD. Intralesional profiling identified CAR T-cell proliferation, tumor-cell death-associated programs, and candidate microenvironmental interactions. These findings warrant further evaluation of this dual-targeting strategy in EMD. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04714827; registered 19 January 2021.

papers.title: Identification of immune- and cellular senescence-related genes in keloids through integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis.
papers.authors: Tian T, Su W, Liao K, Liu Q, Ji R, Yang Z, Hao F.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveKeloids are pathological scars resulting from abnormal connective tissue growth in the skin. Although cellular senescence has been implicated in fibrotic diseases, its role and molecular characteristics in keloids remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify cellular senescence-related genes associated with keloid pathogenesis and investigate their potential relationships with alterations in the immune microenvironment.MethodsPublicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE44270 and GSE92566) and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (GSE181297) from the Gene Expression Omnibus database were integrated for analysis. Cellular senescence-related genes were obtained from the CellAge database and intersected with differentially expressed genes identified between keloid and normal samples to obtain cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes. Protein-protein interaction network analysis was performed to identify hub genes, which were further intersected with single-cell differentially expressed genes to determine key genes. Immune infiltration was assessed using the Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts algorithm, and cellular senescence-associated biological pathways were evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and gene set variation analysis. The expression patterns and cellular distribution of key genes were further evaluated using single-cell sequencing data.ResultsA total of 18 cellular senescence-related differentially expressed genes were identified between keloid and normal samples. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified 10 hub genes, and integration with single-cell transcriptomic data revealed 5 key genes associated with cellular senescence: cyclin D1, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8, galectin 3, and notch receptor 3. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression between keloid and normal groups across the combined bulk-transcriptomic datasets. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated significant associations between key genes and immune cell characteristics. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A was correlated with gamma delta T cells and resting dendritic cells, whereas notch receptor 3 was associated with CD8+ T cells and naive CD4+ T cells. Single-cell analysis further characterized the expression patterns of key genes across different cell populations in keloid tissues.ConclusionThis study provides an integrated transcriptomic and single-cell landscape of cellular senescence-related alterations in keloids. The identified key genes are associated with cellular senescence-related transcriptional changes and immune microenvironment characteristics in keloid tissues. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression patterns at the bulk-transcriptome level, suggesting their relevance in keloid pathogenesis. These findings highlight the potential involvement of cellular senescence-associated programs in the interplay between fibroblast activation and immune alterations in keloids and provide candidate genes for further functional investigation.
papers.venue: The Journal of international medical research

papers.title: Tumor-draining lymph nodes as candidate sources of immunotherapy biomarkers in breast cancer: a multi-omics and artificial intelligence roadmap.
papers.authors: Li Z, Pei S, Qu Z, Zhang L, Lu J, Xian K, Wang J, Fang Y.
papers.abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

papers.title: ID3 endowment and TGFBR2 deletion enhance iPSC-derived CAR macrophage immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Tang C, Tong Y, Han P, Zhao J, Wang X, Song H, Wang M, Liu X, Zhang Q, Zhu Q, Qiang E, Wang W, Chen N, Mo T, Cao Z, Wei Z, An Y, Hui H, T Chung R, Feng X, Zhao W, Gao M, Xiong S, Tian J, Shao T.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies are limited by poor infiltration and immunosuppression in solid tumors. We developed induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived CAR macrophages (CAR-iMac) targeting glypican-3 (GPC3) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), incorporating ID3 endowment and TGFBR2 deletion. Single-cell RNA sequencing associated these modifications with enhanced inflammatory and phagocytic programs and reduced TGF-β responses. In orthotopic HCC preclinical models, magnetic particle imaging (MPI) of labeled CAR-iMac monitored in vivo distribution and persistence, together with histological phenotyping and transcriptional profiling, revealed dose-associated phenotypic state changes to guide dose optimization. The optimized regimen showed antitumor activity and preliminary safety in humanized mice. Additionally, CAR-iMac inhibited orthotopic patient-derived xenograft growth and cooperated with patient-matched T cells in patient-derived HCC organoids to enhance tumor killing and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings supported a scalable macrophage platform integrating functional enhancement, longitudinal cell tracking, and rational dosing.

papers.title: A TCR cup for a TB lipid.
papers.authors: Gapin L.
papers.abstract: Cao et al. (https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20261088) identify a recurrent TRBV7-9 bias among human T cells recognizing mycobacterial phosphomycoketide presented by CD1c. Structural analysis shows how germline-encoded contacts position the receptor to engage the lipid phosphate, linking repertoire bias to a shared recognition strategy.

papers.title: Chemotherapy-induced mast-cell degranulation constrains tertiary lymphoid maturation in lung cancer brain metastasis.
papers.authors: Fu M, You M, Ao Y, Zeng G, Xing Y, Qiu F, Zhang L, Shen Z, Hua W, Mao Y.
papers.abstract: Background Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) support local adaptive immunity and are associated with favorable antitumor responses across multiple cancers. However, how anticancer treatment reshapes TLS maturation, particularly in lung cancer brain metastasis (LCBM), remains poorly understood. Methods We integrated clinicopathological profiling of LCBM cohorts with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial profiling, immune-repertoire analysis, histological validation, and murine intracranial tumor models. Associations between prior treatment and TLS maturation were evaluated using multivariable analyses. Mechanistic studies examined chemotherapy-associated IL-33 release, mast-cell activation, and the effects of PGD2 on antigen-specific T-cell cytotoxicity and B-cell differentiation. Pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS and mast-cell stabilization were further evaluated in vivo. Results Mature TLSs were associated with favorable survival in patients with LCBM, whereas preoperative chemotherapy was independently associated with impaired TLS maturation after adjustment for measured clinical and treatment covariates. Consistent with this observation, chemotherapy-treated tumors exhibited increased IL-33 levels, mast-cell accumulation, and enhanced mast-cell degranulation, with spatial analyses placing activated mast cells within TLS-associated immune niches. Mechanistically, IL-33 activated ST2-expressing mast cells, induced NF-κB-associated transcriptional programs. Functionally, mast cell-derived PGD2 suppressed antigen-specific CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxicity and impaired plasma-cell differentiation, providing a potential link between chemotherapy and weakened local adaptive immunity. In vivo, pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS enhanced chemotherapy efficacy, while mast-cell stabilization with cromolyn sodium reduced chemotherapy-associated degranulation, increased local adaptive immune-cell infiltration, improved intracranial tumor control, and prolonged survival when combined with chemotherapy. Conclusions Our findings support a model in which chemotherapy-associated tissue stress activates an IL-33-responsive mast-cell program and restrains TLS-associated adaptive immunity in LCBM. Although this pathway is unlikely to operate as an exclusively linear or mast-cell-specific mechanism, targeting mast-cell-associated inflammatory signaling may provide a strategy to preserve antitumor immunity and improve the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy in brain metastasis.

papers.title: Hepatocyte Loss of TRMT61A Aggravates Liver Fibrosis by Driving ATF3-Mediated Apoptosis and Macrophage Recruitment.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Wang J, Long XD, Hu ZX, Wo LL, Shao YF, Liu C, Yu QR, Zhou CX, Chen GQ, Wang Q, Zhao Q.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a common pathological consequence of chronic liver injury, but the hepatocyte-intrinsic mechanisms that initiate fibrogenic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify the RNA methyltransferase TRMT61A as a hepatocyte protective factor that is reduced in human fibrotic liver tissues and in experimental mouse models of liver fibrosis. Hepatocyte-specific deletion of Trmt61a was sufficient to trigger liver injury and progressive fibrosis, whereas restoration of enzymatically active TRMT61A restored m 1 A modification and ameliorated fibrosis. Mechanistically, Trmt61a deficiency activated the integrated stress response (ISR) marked by eIF2α phosphorylation and ATF3 induction, promoting hepatocyte apoptosis and CCL2 production. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed profound remodeling of the hepatic immune microenvironment, characterized by loss of embryonically derived Kupffer cells and accumulation of CCR2-positive monocyte-derived macrophages with pro-fibrotic inflammatory programs. Pharmacological CCR2/CCR5 blockade with cenicriviroc or hepatic Atf3 knockdown reduced macrophage infiltration and attenuated fibrosis in Trmt61a-deficient mice. These findings underscore the pivotal role of TRMT61A in regulating hepatocyte fate and remodeling the hepatic immune microenvironment during fibrosis progression, with the ISR-ATF3 axis serving as a central mechanistic hub. Restoring TRMT61A activity in hepatocytes thus represents a promising therapeutic strategy for preserving hepatocyte function and counteracting liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Heparanase-Expressing Regulatory T Cells Drive Immunotherapy Resistance and Poor Outcomes in Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Ozaki R, Mitsuhashi A, Ogino H, Yoshida A, Koyama K, Yabuki Y, Tsukazaki Y, Morita Y, Sato S, Nokihara H, Shinohara T, Hanibuchi M, Takizawa H, Ilan N, Vlodavsky I, Nishioka Y.
papers.abstract: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) and their degrading enzyme heparanase (Hpse) play pivotal roles in tumor invasion and metastasis. Previous studies have reported associations between Hpse expression in tumor cells and patient prognosis. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are a cornerstone of solid tumor therapy, the role of Hpse in antitumor immunity remains unclear. Here, we examined Hpse localization and its impact on the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma. To investigate the relationships among the Hpse expression, tumor prognosis, and tumor-infiltration of immune cells, an immunohistochemical analysis of Hpse1, Hpse2, regulatory T cells (T reg s), macrophages, and CD8 + T cells was performed in resected tumor tissue from lung adenocarcinoma patients. The effects of the Hpse inhibitor PG545 on the invasive capabilities of lymphocytes were investigated. In lung adenocarcinoma tissues, Hpse1 and Hpse2 were expressed in both epithelial tumor cells and immune cells. A high Hpse1 expression and low Hpse2 expression are poor postoperative prognostic factors in both epithelial cells and tumor-infiltrating hematopoietic cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human tumor-infiltrating immune cells revealed that T reg s and some subclusters of macrophages specifically express Hpse1. Lung adenocarcinoma tissue with high Hpse-expressing immune cells demonstrated an increase in tumor-infiltrating T reg s. PG545 suppressed the invasion of T reg s toward the HSPG-containing ECM. Furthermore, PG545 suppressed tumor progression and infiltration of T reg s in a mouse model. In addition, PG545 reinforced antitumor effects of PD-L1 blockade. Hpse expression in T reg s has a significant impact on lung cancer progression and is a promising therapeutic target for novel combination immunotherapy.

papers.title: An X-encoded pyrimidinergic checkpoint: P2Y 4 controls TLR7-IFN-α response in human plasmacytoid dendritic cells.
papers.authors: Rueschpler L, Hennesen J, Herold L, Rosche A, Matschl U, Giesemann-Jansen S, Post S, Diercks BP, Altfeld M, Schloer S.
papers.abstract: Pyrimidinergic molecules such as UTP are released upon cell death and act as damage-associated molecular patterns by activating P2Y receptors, thereby shaping innate immune responses. P2Y receptors have recently been attracting attention as potential therapeutic targets to combat infectious, inflammatory and autoimmune diseases which are increasingly being discovered to affect men and women differently. While sex differences in antiviral immunity have been extensively linked to enhanced IFN-I production in females, sex-specific anti-inflammatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the UTP-responsive, X-chromosomally encoded P2RY4 to be significantly more highly expressed in female pDCs. Single-cell gene expression analysis revealed a female-specific correlation between P2RY4 and Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) expression. Functional interrogation of this axis provided novel insights into the role of P2Y 4 in regulating various cytokines and chemokines, calcium signalling and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) expression. Our findings uncover the nuanced sex differences in P2Y 4 function and propose pyrimidinergic signalling as an overlooked modulator of pDC immunity.

papers.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment.
papers.authors: Wang S, Qian Q, Liu Y, Ding Y, Yang D, Zheng X, Cheng S, Huang G, Gao G, Xiao J, Zhang Z, Jiang S.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition-associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type-specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type-enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

papers.title: RIPK1 inhibition limits expansion of pathogenic double-negative T cells in preclinical autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome models.
papers.authors: Li J, Du Y, Qiu J, Yu X, Li Z, Ma H, Zhang W, Xu X, Li Q, Zhao C, Cao D, Li R, Du Z, Liu H, Zhang X, Fan J, Hu S, He S.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) is an immune disorder characterized by defective lymphocyte apoptosis, leading to lymphoproliferation, autoimmunity, and increased lymphoma risk. Although disease severity correlates with the expansion of double-negative T (DNT) cells, the mechanisms governing their aberrant generation and pathogenicity remain elusive. Through single-cell transcriptomics of peripheral blood from pediatric patients with ALPS, including patients harboring new FAS cell surface death receptor (FAS) mutations ( FAS mutations), we identified a pathogenic effector DNT subset (GRANZYME hi CXCR5 hi ) exhibiting cytotoxic and tissue-infiltrating features, a population conserved in ALPS mouse models. Using an apoptosis-defective murine model that develops early-onset ALPS with robust DNT cell expansion, we found that ALPS-associated caspase-8 functional impairment facilitates receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) activation to drive disease pathogenesis, a process exacerbated by receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) scaffold function. Peripheral CD8 + T cells from both patients with ALPS and mouse models exhibited increased susceptibility to activation-induced conversion into pathogenic DNT cells, which was effectively blocked by RIPK1 inhibition. Mechanistically, RIPK1 activation drove peripheral CD8 + T cells to adopt a pathogenic DNT fate via cAMP-responsive element modulator (CREM)-mediated CD8 silencing. Furthermore, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity reduced DNT cell generation and burden in target organs, reversed cytopenias, and alleviated autoimmune pathology in ALPS mouse models. Our findings establish RIPK1 as a critical driver of ALPS pathogenesis and identify RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: SynAb: Interpretable heavy-light chain synergy modeling for generalizable antibody-antigen interaction prediction.
papers.authors: Cai L, Shi J, Zhang Z, Chen H, Wu Z, Fu X.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen interactions (AAIs) is essential for therapeutic antibody discovery and high-throughput antibody screening. However, existing sequence-based methods often model antibody heavy and light chains independently, overlooking their cooperative contribution to antigen recognition. In this study, we propose SynAb, a synergy-guided cross-attention framework that integrates heavy-light chain regional cooperation into antibody-antigen interaction modeling. SynAb captures cooperative information across antibody functional regions and uses it to guide the interaction between antibody and antigen representations. Experimental results on the HIV and CoV-AbDab datasets demonstrate that SynAb outperforms the evaluated sequence-based methods and exhibits strong generalization in challenging scenarios involving unseen antibodies, unseen antigens, and previously unobserved antibody-antigen pairs. Beyond its predictive performance, SynAb explicitly characterizes the coordinated roles of paired heavy and light chains in antigen recognition. Moreover, without residue-level contact supervision, the model consistently highlights heavy-chain CDR-enriched regions, particularly CDR-H2 and CDR-H3, providing interpretable evidence consistent with established immunological knowledge. Together, these findings establish SynAb as a robust and interpretable framework for sequence-based AAI prediction and a promising computational tool for candidate prioritization in therapeutic antibody screening and synthetic biology applications.

papers.title: Vascularized immunocompetent cortical organoids for modeling human brain development and disease.
papers.authors: Halkoluoto A, Puigdevall Costa P, Weert I, Kauppinen R, Rõlova T, Zunica AR, Trontti K, Kilpinen H, Koistinaho J, Keuters MH, Dhungana H.
papers.abstract: Many current cortical organoid models lack key interacting cell types, including vascular and microglial cells, which are essential for brain tissue function and homeostasis. In this study, we have successfully developed an advanced organoid model through the incorporation of vascular and immune cells. These organoids exhibit capillary-like structures and microglial cells and show neuronal activity as revealed by calcium imaging. This cellular complexity was further confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), which detected neurons, microglial cells, and vascular cells, recapitulating the developmental stage of the fetal transcriptome. In addition, electron microscopy revealed a putative capillary lumen surrounded by endothelial cells. Furthermore, transplantation of these organoids into the mouse brain showed human capillaries in close proximity to mouse capillaries. Taken together, we developed a vascularized, immunocompetent cortical organoid that may serve as a model for studying both neurodegenerative diseases and cerebrovascular dysfunction.

papers.title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species.
papers.authors: Januszyk M, Lu JM, Korah M, Jing SL, Xie PY, Fallah M, Pham B, Guo JL, Berry CE, Wang HH, Talbott HE, Nee K, Le T, Garcia CA, Gonçalves A, Nosrati F, Bauer-Rowe KE, Guo C, Agolia JP, Reveron-Thornton RY, Liang NE, Tomasso A, Kameni LE, DiIorio SE, Parker JBL, Morgan AG, Griffin M, Longacre TA, Foster DS, Wan DC, Norton JA, Delitto D, Longaker MT.
papers.abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation 1 . Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope 2,3 . Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

papers.title: Host-microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues.
papers.authors: López-Sandoval R, Harter MF, Yu Q, Gaspa-Toneu L, Kaltenbach L, Secchia S, Akkerman N, Filip AM, Aubert J, Vasandani SR, Kromer K, Chauvin D, Krishnarajah S, Calvo-Asensio I, Cubela I, Tsiepa S, Almato-Bellavista M, Munteanu S, Fidelin J, Augustin A, Schori C, Bickle M, Bollen Y, Lutolf MP, Recaldin T, Bumann D, Ginhoux F, Hensel M, Beumer J, Nikolaev M, Gjorevski N, Camp JG.
papers.abstract: As a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections. Investigating the human-specific intestinal barrier responses to pathogens is limited by the lack of models integrating the necessary architectural complexity with an autologous immune compartment 1 . Here we developed engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon combining a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. These tissues recapitulate morphological and functional properties that are region specific and compare with those of the native organ. We use the model to characterize the human epithelial response to Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium at the single-cell level, uncovering the distinct gene regulatory networks that underpin luminal versus intracellular pathogen presence. Invaded epithelial cells initiate an IL-18 signalling axis that triggers cytotoxic T cell activation, resulting in epithelial shedding and barrier disruption. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial and immune compartments, providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

papers.title: Butyrate and the brain-gut axis in Parkinson's disease: From microbial metabolite to potential therapeutic target.
papers.authors: Hu J, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with substantial unmet therapeutic needs. This narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the role of the gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acid butyrate in the brain-gut axis in Parkinson's disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies suggest that butyrate reinforces intestinal barrier integrity and modulates intestinal immune responses, with enteric glial and vagal pathways providing possible links to central neuroinflammation. Its effects on microglial inflammatory phenotypes and autophagic clearance of α-synuclein, including possible cholinergic mediation, require further validation. We critically evaluated the strengths and limitations of this evidence, discussed inconsistent findings across cohorts, and summarized clinical studies on butyrate-related interventions, including butyrate supplementation, dietary fiber, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Although preclinical evidence is substantial and context dependent, clinical translation is constrained by small and heterogeneous human cohorts, unresolved butyrate bioavailability, optimal dose and route of administration, long-term safety concerns, variability of the gut microbiota, and the absence of randomized evidence establishing butyrate-specific disease modification. Microglial heterogeneity revealed by single-cell transcriptomic studies also challenges the classical M1/M2 framework. We conclude by proposing priorities for future research, including well-powered randomized trials, standardized butyrate and microbiome measurements, patient stratification, and single-cell investigations.
papers.venue: The Journal of international medical research

papers.title: Single-cell analysis of epithelial transcriptional states identifies stromal associations and candidate targets in colon cancer.
papers.authors: Shi X, Cao X, Guan B, Wu W, Zhu H, Fu Y, Guo X, Wang T.
papers.abstract: Background Colon cancer progression involves coordinated changes in epithelial cells and the tumor microenvironment, yet the transcriptional organization, associated regulatory programs and candidate vulnerabilities of epithelial cell states remain unclear. Methods Multi-cohort single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated with inferred copy-number variation, pseudotime, regulon and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred to characterize state-associated communication. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation, virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to nominate candidates for functional investigation. ZC3HC1 knockdown, overexpression and rescue were assessed in HCT 116 cells using EdU, cell-cycle, apoptosis and migration/invasion assays. Multiplex immunofluorescence examined epithelial and immune-marker distributions in tumor sections. An epithelial-state-informed prognostic model was developed using nested selection within TCGA-COAD and evaluated in GEO cohorts with fixed training-derived thresholds. Results Epithelial cells formed three transcriptional states with distinct expression and regulatory programs. State 3 was enriched for ILF2-, NFYB-, MLX-, CTCF- and HMGA1-associated regulons. Fibroblasts were the dominant signaling source, whereas T cells had the highest incoming communication strength and State 3 showed candidate CypA, COLLAGEN and CD99 expression associations; spatial analyses further showed co-occurrence of collagen ligands with SDC1, SDC4, CD44 and integrin receptor complexes. ZC3HC1 knockdown in HCT 116 cells reduced EdU incorporation, increased G0/G1 accumulation and apoptosis, and diminished migration and invasion; rescue partially restored these phenotypes. Multiplex staining illustrated contrasting myeloid and T-cell distributions around PanCK-positive regions. Virtual screening nominated DB12168 as a candidate ZC3HC1-interacting compound. The epithelial-state-informed risk model showed cohort-dependent prognostic performance, and its associations with immune exclusion and angiogenesis were exploratory. Conclusions Epithelial transcriptional states in colon cancer are associated with distinct regulatory programs and stromal expression patterns. Functional assays implicated ZC3HC1 in HCT 116 cell phenotypes, and virtual screening nominated DB12168 for binding studies, while the epithelial-state-informed risk model provides a framework for retrospective prognostic evaluation.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Transcriptomic Analyses Identify the Regulatory T Cell-Associated Gene MED10 as a Prognostic Predictor in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.authors: Han M, Mao Y, Hu X, Wang J, Sharen G, Cheng H.
papers.abstract: Tregs significantly shape the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, yet the roles of specific Treg-associated genes remain poorly understood. Treg-related genes were screened from scRNA-seq data (GSE161277), followed by expression and prognostic validation in several independent cohorts (TCGA, GSE87211, GSE44076, and GSE17538). GSEA and CellChat characterized regulatory pathways and intercellular communication. MED10 expression was verified in CRC tissues and cell lines by qRT-PCR and western blotting. Functional assays (CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, flow cytometry) evaluated MED10's impact on tumor behavior. Finally, the in vivo relevance of MED10 to tumor growth and immune microenvironmental changes was assessed using a syngeneic mouse model. MED10 was identified as a critical Treg-related gene in CRC, with high expression correlating with shortened survival. GSEA revealed that high MED10 expression was associated with enrichment of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Furthermore, intercellular communication analysis suggested that elevated MED10 expression may be associated with increased interaction strengths between cell populations, potentially contributing to the remodeling of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In vitro functional assays revealed that MED10 knockdown significantly impaired CRC cell proliferation and migration while inducing apoptosis. MED10 knockdown also reduced Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity, which was partially restored by LiCl treatment. Finally, in vivo, MED10 silencing suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by reduced Treg infiltration and enhanced effector T-cell activity. MED10 is associated with CRC progression, Wnt/β-catenin signaling alterations, and a Treg-enriched immunosuppressive immune context, supporting its potential value as a prognostic indicator and candidate therapeutic target.

papers.title: B-cell intrinsic Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein promotes intestinal inflammation by restraining B2 cell-mediated macrophage interleukin-10 responses.
papers.authors: Xu Z, Yuan S, Hu Z, Wu X, Qian J, Gu L, Shi H, Wang X, Su D.
papers.abstract: Background and aims B cells are increasingly recognized as important regulators of intestinal inflammation through both antibody-dependent and antibody-independent mechanisms, but the intrinsic programs controlling inflammatory B-cell functions remain poorly understood. Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein (PTIP) is an essential regulator of B-cell humoral immunity; however, its role in inflammatory B-cell responses remains unclear. Methods We investigated the function of B-cell-intrinsic PTIP using B-cell-specific PTIP-deficient mice and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced experimental colitis. Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein expression was evaluated in murine and human B cells, including analysis of a publicly available human colonic single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset. Antibody-mediated effects, B2-cell-intrinsic activity, and macrophage-associated responses were examined using adoptive transfer, serum transfer, macrophage depletion, and interleukin (IL)-10 pathway blockade approaches. Results PTIP expression was increased in circulating B cells from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and intestinal B cells during DSS-induced colitis. B-cell-specific PTIP deficiency attenuated colitis severity and reduced germinal center B-cell responses and immunoglobulin production. However, adoptive transfer and serum transfer experiments suggested that the protective effect of PTIP deficiency was largely independent of antibody-mediated mechanisms. Transfer of PTIP-deficient conventional B2 cells reduced intestinal inflammation, whereas PTIP-expressing B2 cells promoted disease severity, demonstrating a B2-cell intrinsic function of PTIP. Furthermore, PTIP deficiency enhanced macrophage-associated IL-10 responses, and disruption of macrophage function or IL-10 signaling diminished this protective phenotype. Conclusions PTIP promotes DSS-induced intestinal inflammation by regulating antibody-independent B2-cell inflammatory activity and B2-cell-macrophage communication. These findings identify a previously unrecognized PTIP-dependent immune regulatory pathway linking B-cell intrinsic programs to macrophage-mediated intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Immunopathological mechanisms linking atherosclerosis and ischemic stroke: From microenvironmental vulnerability to precision therapeutics.
papers.authors: Liu W, Zou Q, Liu W, Huang Z.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic ischemic stroke results from a multistage process in which systemic susceptibility and local arterial biology converge to generate plaque vulnerability, thrombosis, embolization, and cerebral ischemia. This review critically integrates experimental, human tissue, observational, imaging, and randomized clinical evidence across this continuum. We distinguish disturbed flow-induced endothelial dysfunction and intimal retention of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins as upstream processes from macrophage dysfunction, defective efferocytosis, vascular smooth muscle cell remodeling, pathological neovascularization, and intraplaque hemorrhage that promote structural vulnerability. We then examine how plaque rupture and, with less direct cerebrovascular evidence, superficial erosion interact with platelet activation, coagulation, and neutrophil-associated immunothrombosis to produce artery-to-artery embolization or hemodynamic ischemia. Systemic modifiers, including clonal hematopoiesis, trained immunity, gut-derived metabolites, psychological stress, infection, and environmental exposures, are evaluated according to evidence maturity and stroke-specific relevance. Poststroke neuroimmune-hematopoietic reprogramming is considered an experimentally supported but incompletely validated feedback mechanism in humans. Among imaging-defined plaque features, carotid intraplaque hemorrhage has comparatively mature human prognostic evidence, whereas many molecular signatures remain investigational. Emerging single-cell, spatial, multiomic, molecular-imaging, and thrombus-profiling technologies are considered separately from clinically validated risk tools. Finally, therapeutic strategies are organized by mechanism and strength of clinical evidence, distinguishing established lipid-lowering, antithrombotic, and reperfusion approaches from investigational inflammatory, lipoprotein(a)-directed, and genome-editing strategies. This evidence-based framework identifies where mechanistic insight is mature, where translation remains uncertain, and how precision prevention may be advanced in atherosclerotic stroke. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Atherosclerotic ischemic stroke is driven by more than arterial narrowing: plaque vulnerability, immune inflammation, thrombosis, and impaired cerebral perfusion interact to determine clinical risk. By separating findings supported by human cerebrovascular evidence from emerging experimental mechanisms, this review clarifies opportunities and limitations for improved risk stratification, biomarker development, and mechanism-guided prevention.
